direction.comments: The direction on a macroscale is an animated musical that takes influence from K-Pop culture and has flavors of demon-hunting anime and other animated films like 'Frozen'; the direction on a microscale is decent as it does give moments personality and gets you to know the cast, though it is not really that deep; the storytelling is pretty nontraditional as the movie basically skips all exposition and resolution as you basically start the story at the end of the journey, with a new conflict introduced; because of how the plot is structured it felt like the first half feels a little rushed as it basically assumes you already know the lore and the backstories for these characters, but the second half feels more like a traditional animated movie

cast.comments: The background voice acting was what you would expect in an animated movie; the vocal performances during the songs were very good and really made the songs well executed and memorable

story.comments: The concept is pretty interesting, as it follows how the concept of demon hunters has gone through different music generations, but the personal struggles for the main character just seem a little too similar to Frozen and other animated movies; The plot structure is a big issue for the movie because they basically cut out the entire exposition and start right when the conflict is introduced, and this kind of makes the first 30 to 40 minutes a little confusing or cringey, but the final hour is more of a traditional plot structure so it is fine; It is very obvious that many scenes were cut, as the movie definitely feels a little rushed and incomplete, but this is something you can expect from an animated movie; The character writing is a big issue for this movie because while the lead and the main Saja Boy are given depth, with the former being a little too similar to Frozen, the remaining characters are basically given no depth, making them pretty forgettable; It feels like they cut out a lot of the depth for the other characters to make the runtime shorter

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is a little cringey in the first 30-40 minutes, but it is decent overall; The dialogue is what you would expect from a family animated movie; The humor is a little cringey in the beginning, but it is still present and has some memorable moments; The symbolism is honestly something we have seen before in other movies as many of the symbols are similar to movies like 'Frozen' and other demon hunting IP; The foreshadowing is kind of what you would expect from a family animated movie, but it is decent overall

score.comments: Mainly interpolations of the soundtrack, which I did enjoy

soundtrack.comments: A true highlight for this movie is that a lot of the songs are catchy and feel like they have their place in the movie to tell the story; My three favorite songs were 'What It Sounds Like,' 'Your Idol', and 'Golden'

editing.comments: Give the movie an Asian animation feel with how it cuts between the cute moments and action sequences

sound.comments: Helps give this movie the pop and kick it needs

animation.comments: Feels very inspired by Asian animation, as the style feels symbolic of this Asian-American film

review.pacing: Pacing is on the faster side, but this is what you would expect from an animated movie; it feels pretty obvious that they cut out a lot of material to make this runtime
review.climax: Climax is executed very well and a true pinnacle for this movie; The climax was definitely my favorite part as it made this movie really worth watching, especially considering it had my favorite song 'What It Sounds Like'
review.tone: Tone is heavily inspired by Asian animation, but has some flavors of family animation you would see in Hollywood
review.final_notes: Went to a sing-along screening at Alamo Drafthouse
review.overall: Overall, a pretty good animated movie that has great animation and a catchy soundtrack, as both show the symbolic blend of Asian and Western influences on this movie; however, 'KPop Demon Hunters' is held back by its poor plot construction and character writing issues, which I feel is because they must have cut out from the runtime
